expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro, one paragraph at tickets.md:92-95: 'An agent sees which tickets are late without working out any due time. A ticket whose due time has passed shows as `OVERDUE` in the ticket list until it is closed. A separate listing returns only the overdue tickets...' (a Status paragraph and a derived-state paragraph follow it). 'Prefix: `TKT`.' at tickets.md:12, 'Prefix: `CLI`.' at cli.md:14. '### Non-goals' at tickets.md:113 with 7 boundaries, e.g. '**No alert.** No command sends a message.' (117) and '**No change to due times.** TKT-005 stays as it is. Business hours, a paused clock, and targets per customer are out of scope.' (119).

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 9 new criteria headed '### PREFIX-NNN: Title': TKT-014..TKT-019 and CLI-010..CLI-012; CLI-001 and CLI-006 edited. check_run: duplicates 0 and testable_lines 0 in both files. Body length, noted not failed: by a rough sentence count 6 of 9 new bodies run past three sentences (TKT-014 5, TKT-017 5, TKT-019 6, CLI-010 4, CLI-011 5, CLI-012 7 with its TODO); mean about 59 words. The edited CLI-006 body is about 119 words.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: cli.md:52 (CLI-006) 'For an overdue ticket, see TKT-014, the line shows `OVERDUE` in place of the state.' Filter: tickets.md:157 (TKT-018) 'The overdue listing returns every overdue ticket and no other ticket.' Order: tickets.md:163 (TKT-019) 'The overdue listing is sorted by due time ascending, so the ticket that was due earliest comes first.' Exact due time: tickets.md:133-134 (TKT-014) 'At the exact due time the ticket is not overdue yet.' Closed: tickets.md:139 (TKT-015) 'A `closed` ticket is never overdue, whatever the time at which it was closed.' Nothing overdue: cli.md:96 (CLI-010) 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.'

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: check_run impl_words=0 in both files; no .py name, function, class, or module in any new or edited body. Outcomes are output lines and exit codes, e.g. CLI-011 'is rejected with a usage error on stderr and exit code 2. Nothing is printed to stdout.' Borderline, not failed: TKT-014 names the time source, 'read from the same clock that stamps events, see LOG-004', and CLI-012's TODO says 'prints a Python traceback', the same wording the existing CLI-007 uses.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: tickets.md:101 'Overdue is derived and never stored. The log and the current time decide it each time a command runs.' tickets.md:149 (TKT-017) 'No event records that a ticket is overdue, and the event kinds stay those of LOG-002. Listing tickets and listing overdue tickets leave the log file unchanged byte for byte, see LOG-001.' No new event kind. INV-001 and INV-002 are not cited by ID (check_run mentions false); the behavior respects both.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-005 reused: tickets.md:132 (TKT-014) 'TKT-005 sets the due time.' and the non-goal at 119 'TKT-005 stays as it is.' List order kept: cli.md:48 (CLI-006) still reads 'prints one line per ticket in ID order, see TKT-013', and the non-goal at tickets.md:123-124 says '`list` gets no filter option and no sort option, and it keeps the order of TKT-013.' The due-time order applies only to the separate overdue listing (TKT-019).

expectations.text: Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.
expectations.evidence: '### Open questions for overdue tickets' ends tickets.md (line 171) with 8 TODO items, each naming the criteria that rest on it, e.g. 187: 'TODO: confirm that a ticket is not overdue at the exact due time. TKT-014 assumes it.' and 188: 'TODO: confirm that tickets with an equal due time fall back to ID order. TKT-019 assumes it.' They match the 8 questions in questions.md one to one. No mark sits at the criteria themselves except CLI-006 'This rule is a draft and is not built.' and the TODO under CLI-012 (cli.md:113); TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-019 and CLI-010 state the assumed answer plainly. Not silent, because the in-spec list names each of them. Bar used for all six runs: an assumption counts as marked when the spec itself flags it and ties it to the criterion, by a mark under the criterion or by an in-spec list entry that names the criterion ID.

expectations.text: Skim test: the intro paragraph's first sentence says what the feature is for a support agent; each criterion title names the behavior; no lead is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: Intro first sentence, tickets.md:92: 'An agent sees which tickets are late without working out any due time.' It says what the feature does for the agent. Titles name behaviors ('A closed ticket is never overdue', 'Assigning does not change overdue', 'Overdue is never recorded', 'overdue takes no arguments', 'overdue on a log that cannot be read'); 'CLI-010: overdue' is a bare command name in the repo's style (CLI-006: list), and 'The overdue listing' is a label. Every new paragraph lead states a claim; a sweep with the TODO/Status prefixes stripped gives 0 teaser findings. Status leads at cli.md:8 and cli.md:89 are claims, not teasers.
